pc_imem: The address of the instruction to fetch. Every cycle starts here.
pc_add: The same PC value, fanned out to the adder that works out the next sequential address.
four: Hard-wired 4. Every MIPS instruction is 4 bytes, so the next one sits 4 bytes on.
pc4_mux: The default next PC: the instruction right after this one.
pc4_badd: Branch offsets are counted from PC+4, not from the PC of the branch itself.
pc4_hi: The top 4 bits of PC+4 become the top of the jump address, so a jump stays inside the current 256 MB region.
instr: The 32-bit word fetched from instruction memory. The fields below are split off by wiring alone: no logic, just different traces taking different bits.
f_op: 6 bits that tell Control which kind of instruction this is.
f_rs: Picks the register read on Read data 1.
f_rt: Picks the register read on Read data 2.
f_rt_mux: For lw, rt names the destination register.
f_rd: For R-type instructions, rd names the destination register.
f_imm: The 16-bit constant of lw, sw and beq: an offset in bytes (lw, sw) or in words (beq).
f_funct: For R-type, funct says which operation: 100000 add, 100010 sub, 100100 and, 100101 or, 101010 slt.
f_target: The 26-bit word address of a jump.
wr: Which register is written at the clock edge (only if RegWrite = 1).
rd1: The value of register rs. It is always the ALU's first operand.
rd2_mux: The value of rt, as the ALU's second operand (R-type and beq).
rd2_mem: Read data 2 → Data memory write data
The value of rt, which sw stores into memory.
sext_mux: The 16-bit immediate widened to 32 bits by copying bit 15 into the top 16 bits, so a negative offset stays negative.
sext_shl: The branch offset, still counted in words.
alub: Whichever operand ALUSrc picked: Read data 2, or the sign-extended immediate.
res_mem: For lw and sw the ALU adds base + offset: this is the memory address.
res_mux: For R-type the ALU result is what gets written back.
zero: 1 when the ALU result is 0. beq subtracts rs − rt, so Zero = 1 means the two registers are equal.
mem_rd: The word read from memory. It is only driven when MemRead = 1.
wd: The value written into the register file at the clock edge.
shl_badd: Shifting left by 2 turns a word offset into a byte offset.
btarget: PC+4 + offset × 4: where beq goes if it is taken.
pcsrc: 1 only for a beq whose two registers are equal. It steers the PCSrc mux.
m1: PC+4, or the branch target if the branch is taken.
jtarget: The 26-bit target shifted left 2: a byte address inside the current region.
jaddr: PC+4 [31–28] joined in front of target × 4. Joining wires is free: no gate does it.
next: Loaded into the PC at the clock edge. This loop back to the PC is what makes the processor move on.
c_RegDst: Chooses the destination register: 0 = rt [20–16], 1 = rd [15–11].
c_Jump: 1 makes the next PC the jump address.
c_Branch: 1 for beq. It is ANDed with Zero to decide whether to branch.
c_MemRead: 1 lets data memory drive Read data.
c_MemtoReg: Chooses what is written back: 0 = ALU result, 1 = memory read data.
c_ALUOp: Tells ALU control what to do: 00 add, 01 subtract, 10 look at funct.
c_MemWrite: 1 writes Read data 2 into memory at the clock edge.
c_ALUSrc: Chooses ALU input B: 0 = Read data 2, 1 = sign-extended immediate.
c_RegWrite: 1 writes Write data into Write register at the clock edge.
alu_op: ALU control's decision: 0000 and, 0001 or, 0010 add, 0110 sub, 0111 slt.

pc: A 32-bit register: the processor's only record of where it is. It changes only at the rising clock edge, when it loads Next PC.
four: A hard-wired value. No logic at all.
add4: A dedicated adder, so the ALU stays free. Its output is ready early in the cycle.
imem: Read-only while the program runs. Address in, 32-bit instruction out, with no clock involved: it behaves like combinational logic.
ctrl: Turns the 6-bit opcode into every control line (amber). It is a truth table in hardware: same opcode, same outputs, every time.
regs: 32 registers of 32 bits. Two read ports answer at once (combinational); the one write port only acts at the clock edge, and only when RegWrite = 1. Register 0 always reads 0.
sext: 16 bits in, 32 out: bit 15 is copied into bits 31–16. Only wires, no gates.
shlj: 26 bits in, 28 out: two zeros appended. Only wires.
shlb: Multiplies the word offset by 4. Only wires.
aluctl: Combines ALUOp (from Control) with funct (from the instruction) into the 4-bit ALU operation. This two-level decoding keeps the main Control unit small.
badd: Computes PC+4 + offset×4 every cycle, whether or not the instruction is a branch.
alu: Adds, subtracts, ANDs, ORs or sets-less-than, as ALU operation says. Also raises Zero when the result is 0.
and: PCSrc = Branch AND Zero. With Branch = 0 the Zero flag cannot matter.
dmem: Reads when MemRead = 1; writes at the clock edge when MemWrite = 1. Address from the ALU, write data from Read data 2.
mRegDst: 5-bit mux: which field names the register to write. Lever points at the input that passes through.
mALUSrc: 32-bit mux: ALU input B is Read data 2 (0) or the sign-extended immediate (1).
mMemtoReg: 32-bit mux: write back the ALU result (0) or memory read data (1).
mPCSrc: 32-bit mux: next sequential PC (0) or branch target (1).
mJump: 32-bit mux: the PCSrc mux output (0) or the jump address (1). Its output goes back to the PC.
step: Press it to deliver one rising clock edge. On a real board a crystal does this 25 million times a second.

MemWrite.j: 0 · must be 0, or memory is clobbered

RegWrite.sw: 0 · must be 0, or a register is clobbered
RegWrite.beq: 0 · must be 0, or a register is clobbered
